Just posted a similar list over at /r/Android today. I'm an Android "power user" in that I like to take advantage of Android's Linux core and use it for Linuxy things. My must-have app list includes:

  • Custom Recovery (TWRP preferred)

  • Custom ROM (CyanogenMod 12.1 preferred)

  • F-Droid (open source app repository)

  • Hacker's Keyboard (full function keyboard with control and modifier keys)

  • AdAway (hosts file ad blocker)

  • Terminal Emulator (access the Linux shell)

  • XServer XSDL (X server for Linux UIs to run in)

  • busybox (included with most custom ROMs, provides a lot of Linux command line utilities)

  • ES File Manager (powerful file browser with root access and many network protocols supported)

  • Debian rootfs (combined with chroot from busybox, XServer XSDL, and Terminal Emulator means pocket Debian machine)

  • ssh client (in Debian, to access my other Linux machines both in command line and with X forwarding to XServer XSDL)

  • openvpn client (in Debian, to connect to my router-hosted VPN and connect to my home computers/LAN from anywhere)

  • Firefox Nightly (best browser on Android, nightly so I get latest updates and developer features like unofficial plugins support)

  • VLC (plays anything and is open source)

  • Kodi (formerly XBMC) (also a good media player that is open source)

  • CalcTunes (an in-progress app I'm working on, might spin off my most used feature into a separate app for release, which is the ability to download music in any transcoded format desired from a Subsonic [or compatible] server and save to anywhere on the phone, SD card, or attached USB disk)

  • AndieGraph (TI calculator emulator, gives you TI-83 and TI-86 [among others] that work perfectly and has a nice UI, use this for work all the time)

Asti Media Player - allows you to play a video in the background with the screen off and whilst you do different things, has better performance than VLC whilst also supporting a wide range of video and audio formats.

UC Browser - I've used this web browser since I had my first Nokia java phone in 2003 and it just gets better and better. Chrome and Firefox are shit in my opinion, they didn't seem to put much effort into them or try to make them proper mobile browsers. Even though it's a version for your phone it would be best used with a keyboard and mouse, quite disappointed I was. For a proper MOBILE browser, UC is the light and the way.

Multi tabbed, drag and drop, sorting out your file system is a breeze, also has support for various online storage accounts and connecting with your pc (which I haven't tried). The only other file browser worthy of a mention that does something different is X-plore. Lots of features, I just found it personally difficult to use.

Other then that it's really just about looking around for what suits you best (I guess anything I've mentioned is though).
